overview.title: Private language models, run on DHBW hardware — in the browser and via API
overview.intro: This service pools DHBW's LLM resources behind one shared, <1>OpenAI-compatible endpoint</1> — usable with any tool that accepts a base URL and an API key.
overview.introChat: Chatting needs no key: the DHBW chat runs right in the browser.
overview.promise: Requests are not stored and never leave DHBW; nothing is passed to commercial providers. Tiered quotas per person keep the sharing fair.

signIn.title: 1 · Sign in
signIn.a: Sign in with the DHBW account
signIn.b: The quota follows from the access rule

key.title: 2 · Get an API key
key.a: One API key per device or project
key.c: Deletable at any time without touching the others

use.title: 3 · Use it
use.a: Works with VS Code, the OpenAI SDK, Continue, Zed, curl
use.b: Stable model names: chat-default, chat-fast, code
use.c: The pool absorbs failures by itself

models.title: Which model names are stable
models.stable: Use the neutral names <1>{{names}}</1>. They stay valid and always point to whatever is best available right now.
models.concrete: The model list also contains the concrete model names of the participating machines. These <1>can disappear at any time</1> — when a GPU is needed for a course or a different model is loaded. Anything meant to outlive a session should therefore use the neutral names.

tools.title: What it works with
tools.hint: Any tool that accepts an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Enter the base URL and your API key there. The linked guides come from the projects themselves.
tools.ownCode: For your own programs: <1>examples for the OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex and curl</1> in the LiteLLM documentation.

description.vscode: Copilot Chat with a custom endpoint, no subscription — guide and ready-made JSON when creating an API key
description.continue: Code assistant for VS Code and JetBrains
description.cherry: Chat for macOS, Windows and Linux
description.msty: Chat with a side-by-side view of several models

vscode.title: For VS Code (GitHub Copilot Chat)
vscode.scope: Built in since VS Code 1.122, no GitHub account or Copilot subscription needed. Applies to chat and agent mode, not to inline completions.

steps.palette: Open the command palette (<2>⇧⌘P</2> or <3>Ctrl+Shift+P</3>) and choose <1>Chat: Manage Language Models</1>.
steps.add: <1>Add Models</1> → <1>Custom Endpoint</1>. Enter <2>DHBW</2> as the name, paste the API key from above, API type <1>Chat Completions</1>.
steps.json: Click the gear next to <1>DHBW</1> — the file <2>chatLanguageModels.json</2> opens. In the “DHBW” entry, replace <3>"models": [ … ]</3> with the JSON below; keep the API key line. Save.
steps.select: Pick the model <1>DHBW Code</1> at the top of the chat window.

vscode.keepIds: Do not change the model names: <2>"id"</2> must be exactly code, chat-default or chat-fast.

keys.title: API keys
keys.count: at most {{max}} at a time · {{own}} in use
keys.chatNotCounted: the DHBW chat key does not count
keys.full: Limit reached — delete an old key before creating a new one.
keys.name: Name
keys.deleteMessage: “{{name}}” stops working immediately. Programs using it get errors from then on.
keys.deleteChatMessage: The DHBW chat key is created again at the next chat sign-in. Running chats fail until then.
keys.onceText: This API key is never shown again — store it now.
keys.shellHint: Both lines together — many tools read exactly these two variables.

usage.live: Values come live from the gateway.
usage.perKeyHint: Each API key has its own short-term budget; the monthly quota is shared by all.

explain.units: <1>Units:</1> spend and budgets are accounting units, not euros. Every model has an internal price per token (input and output separately), which gives the cost of each request. That way long and short requests can be weighed fairly.
explain.monthly: <1>Monthly quota:</1> everything spent across all of the account's API keys (including the DHBW chat) since the last reset. Once it is used up, requests are refused until the reset.
explain.shortTerm: <1>Short-term spend:</1> a smaller budget per API key for the given period (e.g. 4 h). It keeps a runaway loop from using up the whole monthly quota at once and is fully available again after the reset. 0.0000 therefore means nothing spent since the last reset — not that the key was never used.

scriptsTip.current: The scripts on the machine match what the service ships.
scriptsTip.outdated: The machine runs an older version and fetches the new one at its next check-in. Normal for up to an hour after a rollout — it reports the version from before that run's update.
scriptsTip.heldBack: Older version, on purpose: the rollout currently reaches only the canary devices. Arrives once that list is emptied.
scriptsTip.unknown: The machine does not report its version — its scripts predate the report. Resolves with the next update.

adminUi.title: LiteLLM admin UI
adminUi.hint: Models, sites, spend history, team management — signs in automatically.

jamf.title: Enrol Macs via JAMF
jamf.hint: One profile, one package, one policy — identical for every device. No script parameter, no device variable, no list of serial numbers.

profile.title: 1 · Configuration profile
profile.hint: Contains the enrolment address and token. JAMF: Computers → Configuration Profiles → Upload, scope to the device group. The three fields are optional and apply to every device in scope — use one profile per group for several sites. Downloading the same profile again yields the same UUID and replaces the existing one.
profile.secret: The profile carries the token of the whole fleet: do not pass it on by mail or ticket, delete it locally after the upload to JAMF.

package.title: 2 · Package and policy
package.deleteHint: Only removes the download from the service. Nothing changes on the devices or in JAMF. Upload again with build-bundle.sh --upload.
package.deleteMessage: {{file}} is removed from the service. The devices are not affected.
package.missing: No package is stored in the service yet. Operations uploads it with <2>fleet/macos/build-bundle.sh --upload</2>.
package.policy:
Settings → Packages → Upload
Policy:  Packages → Install  (package above)
Trigger: Recurring Check-in
Execution Frequency: Once per computer
Scope:   the same device group as the profile
package.hint: No script in the policy, no parameters. The order of profile and package does not matter: if the package comes first, the first run exits 0 and the hourly check-in completes the enrolment later. The package (identifier <2>{{id}}</2>) installs files under /usr/local/libexec/dhbw-llm/ and sets up the check-in service.
package.allowList: <1>Note:</1> enrolment is limited to {{count}} approved serial numbers — new devices must first be listed in the inventory (<2>fleet.allowedSerials</2>).

net.title: 3 · Network
net.hint: Both currently IPv6 only — in an IPv4-only network enrolment fails. Requires Apple Silicon with at least 16 GB.

check.title: 4 · Verify
check.hint: After the check-in the device appears in the table below within minutes (at the latest after {{minutes}} minutes). On the device: enrolment, handshake (under 2 minutes), GPU (must show Metal, not cpu):

updates.title: Updates

explain.off: Scripts come only from the package — a patch means a new package via JAMF.
explain.all: At every hourly check-in the Macs compare their scripts with the service's version and replace what differs. A patch needs no new package.
explain.canary: Staged: only the canary devices get the current version; all others keep theirs until the canary list is emptied.

updates.root: A new package is only needed when the WireGuard binaries change. This lets the service run code as root on the devices; JAMF remains the way back if a patch fails.

machines.title: Device fleet
machines.assignment: What runs on which machine follows from its memory class; exceptions per serial number live in the inventory (<2>fleet.overrides</2>). Takes effect at the next hourly check-in.
machines.pathsTitle: Check-in and inference are two separate paths
machines.paths: <1>Check-in</1> is the control path: every hour the machine calls the enrolment endpoint over public HTTPS and fetches its assignment. “Silent” means that has not happened for three intervals. <1>Inference</1> is the data path: whether LiteLLM reached the machine through the tunnel at the last health check. <1>Paused</1> is not a failure: someone is working at the machine, so it stopped its inference service and gets no requests.

linux.title: Enrol Linux machines without device management
linux.hint: Run as root on the machine. It generates its own key pair, enrols, and sets up two systemd timers. This does <1>not</1> install an inference service — the site keeps running its own; it only has to listen on the tunnel address.
linux.options: Optional: <2>--operator "Labor WI"</2> (group the machine belongs to, <1>not</1> an address), <2>--port 8000</2> for vLLM instead of Ollama, <2>--gate always</2> for a dedicated machine.
linux.secret: The command contains the enrolment token of the whole fleet — it does not belong in a ticket or a chat.

stateTip.blocked: Blocked centrally: the machine is refused and not part of the pool.
stateTip.silent: No check-in at the enrolment endpoint for {{since}}. Says nothing about the tunnel — the Inference column does.
stateTip.active: The machine checks in hourly and last did so on schedule.

inferenceTip.reachable: LiteLLM reached this machine through the tunnel at the last health check.
inferenceTip.failing: No deployment on this machine answers: {{error}}
inferenceTip.partial: Only some of its models answer: {{error}}
inferenceTip.paused: Intended: someone is working at the machine, so it paused its inference service. Comes back by itself once nobody is signed in.
inferenceTip.unregistered: LiteLLM does not know this machine. The sync runs every five minutes and only adds machines that currently answer.
inferenceTip.unknown: LiteLLM's health data could not be fetched.

fleet.primaryIpTip: The machine's own address in its local network (interface of the default route), reported at its last enrolment. Behind NAT this is not the address it appears under from outside.
fleet.directTip: Connected without a tunnel. Protection then rests solely on the endpoint's API key, no longer on the network topology.
fleet.externalTip: This machine runs its own inference service — its model cannot be switched from here. Shown is what it serves.
fleet.differsTip: Assigned is {{model}}, present is something else: the agent did not apply the assignment.
fleet.blockTip: The machine is refused and stays refused — even if it enrols again. Its entry and address are kept. This is the way for a stolen or misbehaving device.
fleet.unblockTip: Lift the block: the machine is admitted again at its next check-in and keeps its address.
fleet.forgetTip: Delete the entry and free the address. This does NOT keep the machine out — if it checks in again it is enrolled with a new address. To keep it out: block it.
fleet.forgetMessage: {{name}} ({{serial}}) is removed from the fleet and its address freed. If the machine checks in again it is enrolled anew — block it instead to keep it out.

access.title: Access rules
access.hint: Who may use the LLM service, with which role and quota. People and groups come from the role-provider. Without a matching rule there is no access — not to the chat either.
access.bootstrapTip: Admins from the configuration. They make sure someone can always maintain this list and cannot be changed here.
access.deleteMessage: The rule for {{token}} is deleted. Anyone who had access only through it loses it within a few minutes.

how.none: <1>No rule, no access.</1> That applies to API keys and the DHBW chat alike.
how.highest: <1>Several rules:</1> the highest role wins; for equal roles a person rule (<2>user:</2>) beats a group rule (<2>group:</2>).
how.roles: <1>Roles:</1> “Use” may create keys and use the chat, “Fleet management” may also look after the device fleet, “Administration” may also maintain these rules.

access.tokenInvalid: Please enter a token of the form user:<email> or group:<id>.
access.gpuTierHint: Access to GPU environments and JupyterHub; the tier sets how many GPUs can be used at the same time.

noAccess.title: No access to the LLM service
noAccess.text: There is no access rule for this account. Access is granted by the service's administrators.
noAccess.page: This page is not available for this role.
